subject: SCI
title: Science 1 (NGSS)
description: First-grade science follows the California NGSS: students investigate how vibrations make sound and how light lets us see, cast shadows, and pass through materials, then design devices that communicate with light and sound. They track patterns of the sun, moon, stars and daylight, explore how plant and animal parts help them survive (and inspire human inventions), and compare parents and offspring. Every unit includes hands-on investigations with household materials and simple engineering design challenges.
framework: California Next Generation Science Standards; 2016 CA Science Framework

standards.1-PS4-1: Plan and conduct investigations to provide evidence that vibrating materials can make sound and that sound can make materials vibrate.
standards.1-PS4-2: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account that objects in darkness can be seen only when illuminated.
standards.1-PS4-3: Plan and conduct investigations to determine the effect of placing objects made with different materials in the path of a beam of light.
standards.1-PS4-4: Use tools and materials to design and build a device that uses light or sound to solve the problem of communicating over a distance.
standards.1-LS1-1: Use materials to design a solution to a human problem by mimicking how plants and/or animals use their external parts to help them survive, grow, and meet their needs.
standards.1-LS1-2: Read texts and use media to determine patterns in behavior of parents and offspring that help offspring survive.
standards.1-LS3-1: Make observations to construct an evidence-based account that young plants and animals are like, but not exactly like, their parents.
standards.1-ESS1-1: Use observations of the sun, moon, and stars to describe patterns that can be predicted.
standards.1-ESS1-2: Make observations at different times of year to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year.
standards.K-2-ETS1-1: Ask questions, make observations, and gather information about a situation people want to change to define a simple problem that can be solved through a new or improved object or tool.
standards.K-2-ETS1-2: Develop a simple sketch, drawing, or physical model to illustrate how the shape of an object helps it function as needed to solve a given problem.
standards.K-2-ETS1-3: Analyze data from tests of two objects designed to solve the same problem to compare the strengths and weaknesses of how each performs.

resources.name: PBS LearningMedia – Science

units.title: Scientists and Engineers at Work
units.big_idea: Scientists ask questions about the world; engineers solve problems by designing, testing and improving.

units.title: Sound and Vibration
units.big_idea: Sound is made by vibrating objects, and sound can make things vibrate.

units.title: Light, Darkness and Shadows
units.big_idea: We see objects only when light shines on them; materials let all, some, or no light through.

units.title: Patterns in the Sky: Sun, Moon and Stars
units.big_idea: The sun, moon and stars move across the sky in patterns we can predict.

units.title: Daylight and the Seasons
units.big_idea: The amount of daylight changes in a pattern through the year.

units.title: Plant and Animal Parts: Nature as Inventor
units.big_idea: Plants and animals have external parts that help them survive, and people copy those ideas to solve problems.

units.title: Animal Parents and Their Young
units.big_idea: Parents and offspring behave in ways that help the young survive.

units.title: Like Parent, Like Offspring
units.big_idea: Young plants and animals are like, but not exactly like, their parents.

units.title: Engineering Showcase and Year Review
units.big_idea: Science ideas help us design solutions to real problems.

weeks.topic: What scientists do: observing and asking questions
objectives: Use senses and tools to observe
Ask testable questions

days.title: Five senses walk
days.work: Take a backyard or park walk and record one thing you see, hear, smell and touch in a science notebook.

days.title: Magnifier lab
days.work: Observe a leaf, rock and shell with a magnifying glass; draw and label details you couldn't see before.

days.title: Question jar
days.work: Write or dictate 5 'I wonder' questions about nature and sort them into 'can test' and 'look up'.

days.title: Mystery bag
days.work: Identify 4 hidden objects by touch only and describe the clues you used.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain to a family member how scientists observe and ask questions, using your notebook drawings.

weeks.assessment: Science notebook observation entries with labeled drawings.

weeks.topic: What engineers do: defining problems and designing
objectives: Define a simple problem
Sketch and build a solution

days.title: Problems around us
days.work: Read about engineers (e.g., 'Rosie Revere, Engineer' by Andrea Beaty, library) and list 3 problems at home that a tool could fix.

days.title: Define the problem
days.work: Problem: a toy needs to cross a 20 cm 'river' between two books; draw the problem.

days.title: Sketch
days.work: Sketch two bridge designs and label the materials.

days.title: Build
days.work: Build your favorite design from paper and craft sticks.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Test whether the toy can cross; tell what worked and what you would change.

weeks.assessment: Design sketch and oral explanation of the problem and solution.

objectives: Test two designs and compare data
Improve a design

days.title: Foil boats
days.work: Shape two 15 cm squares of foil into two different boat designs (flat raft and tall-sided tub) and sketch each.

days.title: Test
days.work: Add pennies one at a time to each boat until it sinks; record counts in a table.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare data: which shape held more pennies and why?

days.title: Improve
days.work: Redesign the weaker boat by changing one feature (wider base or taller sides) and retest it with pennies.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw the engineering cycle (ask, imagine, plan, create, improve) with your boat as the example.

weeks.assessment: Data table and engineering cycle drawing.

objectives: Show that vibrating materials make sound

days.title: Feel your voice
days.work: Hum with fingers on your throat; hum loud and soft and describe the vibrations.

days.title: Ruler twang
days.work: Hang a ruler off a table and twang it at different lengths; record what you see and hear.

days.title: Rubber band guitar
days.work: Stretch rubber bands over a tissue box; pluck and observe the vibrations.

days.title: Sound walk
days.work: List 10 sounds around the house and what is vibrating to make each one.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw and label how a sound is made, using the word vibrate.

weeks.assessment: Labeled drawing explaining vibration and sound.

objectives: Show that sound can make materials vibrate

days.title: Dancing rice
days.work: Stretch plastic wrap over a bowl, sprinkle rice, bang a pan nearby and watch the rice jump.

days.title: Spoon and water
days.work: Strike a metal spoon and touch it to water; observe ripples.

days.title: Your ears
days.work: Watch a short PBS clip about how ears hear; model an eardrum with plastic wrap.

days.title: Plan an investigation
days.work: Plan how to test whether louder sounds make rice jump higher; carry it out.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain your evidence that sound makes materials vibrate.

weeks.topic: Loud and soft, high and low
objectives: Investigate volume and pitch

days.title: Water jars
days.work: Tap jars with different water levels; order them from high to low pitch.

days.title: Band thickness
days.work: Pluck thick and thin rubber bands; record pitch.

days.title: Loud vs. soft
days.work: Pluck gently and strongly; compare vibration size.

days.title: Make a song
days.work: Play a short tune on your water-jar xylophone.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Pitch and volume sort quiz with picture cards.

objectives: Design a device that uses sound to communicate

days.title: History of sound signals
days.work: Learn how drums, bells and whistles sent messages long ago.

days.title: Cup phone
days.work: Build a cup-and-string telephone and test talking across a room.

days.title: Test materials
days.work: Compare string, yarn and wire for the cup phone; record which works best.

days.title: Signal code
days.work: Create a 3-beat drum code for messages and test it outside.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain how the vibrations travel in your cup phone.

objectives: Explain the relationship between sound and vibration

days.title: Mystery Science
days.work: Watch a free Mystery Science sound lesson and answer the mystery question.

days.title: Instrument design
days.work: Design and build a new instrument from household materials.

days.title: Compare instruments
days.work: Compare your instrument with another; which is louder? higher?

days.title: Concert
days.work: Play your instrument and explain what vibrates.

days.title: Unit 2 check
days.work: Complete a sound assessment: draw what vibrates in 3 instruments and answer short questions about loud/soft and high/low sounds.

weeks.topic: We see when there is light
objectives: Explain that objects in darkness can only be seen when illuminated
materials: shoebox with a peephole and a lid flap

days.title: Light sources
days.work: Sort pictures into light sources (sun, lamp, fire) and non-sources (mirror, moon).

days.title: Peep box
days.work: Look into a closed shoebox with a toy inside; then open a flap to let light in and compare.

days.title: Dark room
days.work: Sit in a dark closet and record what you can and cannot see; add light gradually.

days.title: Evidence talk
days.work: Explain why we need light to see, using your peep-box observations.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw what you saw in the box with and without light.

objectives: Test what happens when materials are placed in a light beam
materials: plastic wrap, wax paper, cardboard, fabric, foil

days.title: Predict
days.work: Predict which materials will let light through.

days.title: Test
days.work: Shine a flashlight through each material onto a wall and record results.

days.title: Sort
days.work: Sort materials into transparent, translucent, opaque.

days.title: Home hunt
days.work: Find 3 transparent, 3 translucent and 3 opaque objects at home and test each with the flashlight.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain why window glass is transparent and curtains are opaque.

objectives: Explain how shadows form
Change shadow size and shape

days.title: Shadow puppets
days.work: Make hand-shadow animals on a wall with a flashlight and explain that your hand blocks the light.

days.title: Size change
days.work: Move a toy closer and farther from the light; measure shadow size.

days.title: Outdoor shadows
days.work: Trace your shadow with chalk at 9 a.m. and again at noon.

days.title: Shadow puppet theater
days.work: Make cardboard shadow puppets on sticks and perform a short shadow show behind a bedsheet lit by a lamp.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain why a shadow forms when an opaque object blocks light.

objectives: Investigate how mirrors redirect light

days.title: Mirror bounce
days.work: Bounce a flashlight beam off a mirror to hit a target.

days.title: Shiny vs. dull
days.work: Compare reflection from foil, mirror and paper.

days.title: Periscope
days.work: Build a simple periscope from a milk carton and two mirrors.

days.title: Mirror maze
days.work: Use two mirrors to redirect light around a corner.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw arrows showing light's path in your mirror maze.

objectives: Design a light device to communicate over distance

days.title: Lighthouses
days.work: Read about lighthouses and how ships use them.

days.title: Flashlight code
days.work: Invent a flashlight blink code and send messages.

days.title: Color filters
days.work: Use colored cellophane for different signals.

days.title: Test outdoors
days.work: Test your flashlight code at dusk from across the yard; record which messages a partner decoded correctly.

days.title: Unit 3 check
days.work: Complete a light assessment (sort materials, draw a shadow, explain seeing in the dark) and explain how your signal device works.

weeks.topic: The sun's path across the sky
objectives: Observe and describe the sun's daily pattern
Use the pattern to make predictions

days.title: Sun safety and landmarks
days.work: Learn never to look directly at the sun; stand in the same spot and sketch where the sun is above a tree, roof or pole at 9 a.m.

days.title: Three sky sketches
days.work: Sketch the sun's position from the same spot at morning, noon and late afternoon, labeling east and west with a compass.

days.title: Chalk shadow tracing
days.work: Stand on an X in the driveway and have someone trace your shadow at 9 a.m., noon and 3 p.m.; compare length and direction.

days.title: Pattern talk
days.work: Use your sketches and tracings to describe the pattern (rises in the east, highest at midday, sets in the west) in two sentences.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Predict and draw where the sun and your shadow will be at noon tomorrow, then check your prediction outside.

weeks.assessment: Prediction drawing checked against a real observation.

objectives: Use shadows to track the sun's movement
Predict shadow positions

days.title: Build a sundial
days.work: Push a pencil through the center of a paper plate, anchor it with clay in a sunny spot, and point the plate's '12' mark north.

days.title: Mark the hours
days.work: Every hour from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., mark the pencil's shadow on the plate and write the clock time beside it.

days.title: Predict and test
days.work: Before checking, predict where tomorrow's 10 a.m. shadow will fall; place a coin there and see if the shadow lands on it.

days.title: Sundial vs. clock
days.work: Read the time from your sundial and from a clock at 3 different times; record both in a table.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain to a family member why the shadow moves (the sun's position changes) using your plate as evidence.

weeks.assessment: Sundial with hourly marks and a correct oral explanation.

objectives: Observe and record the moon's shape over time
materials: sandwich cookies and a plastic knife

days.title: Start a moon journal
days.work: Go outside after dinner and draw the moon's shape and position in a calendar-style journal; continue nightly for four weeks.

days.title: Read The Moon Book
days.work: Read Gail Gibbons' 'The Moon Book' and list the names of 4 moon shapes (phases).

days.title: Cookie phases
days.work: Scrape frosting from sandwich cookies to model new, crescent, half and full moons; label them on a paper plate.

days.title: Daytime moon
days.work: Look for the moon in the morning or afternoon sky and record the time and shape; discuss why it can be seen in daytime.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Put 6 moon-phase picture cards in order and compare them with your journal so far.

weeks.assessment: Moon-phase card order and journal entries.

objectives: Explain that the moon's shape changes in a repeating pattern
Predict the next shape
materials: ball on a stick (foam ball and pencil)

days.title: Journal check
days.work: Lay out two weeks of moon drawings and describe how the lit part is growing (waxing) or shrinking (waning).

days.title: Lamp-and-ball model
days.work: In a dark room, hold a foam ball at arm's length and turn slowly around a lamp; watch the lit part change like moon phases.

days.title: NASA Space Place
days.work: Explore a NASA Space Place moon activity and add one new fact about the moon to your journal.

days.title: Predict
days.work: Using the pattern, draw what you think the moon will look like in 3 nights; check it when the day comes.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain in 2–3 sentences that the moon's pattern repeats about every month, pointing to your journal as evidence.

weeks.assessment: Prediction accuracy and written pattern explanation.

objectives: Observe that many stars are seen at night but not during the day
Recognize a constellation
materials: black construction paper and a pushpin

days.title: Stargazing count
days.work: On a clear night, look at the sky for 5 minutes, count visible stars in one window pane's view, and record the time.

days.title: Why not in daytime?
days.work: Shine a flashlight on the wall in a dark room, then in a bright sunny room; explain how sunlight hides the stars.

days.title: Constellation viewer
days.work: Poke the Big Dipper pattern into the bottom of a paper cup and shine a flashlight through it onto the ceiling.

days.title: Find the Big Dipper
days.work: Use your cup map to search for the Big Dipper in the northern sky; draw what you find.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer: 'Are stars still there during the day? How do you know?' using your flashlight evidence.

weeks.assessment: Star count record and evidence-based answer.

objectives: Use observations to describe predictable patterns of the sun, moon and stars

days.title: Data review
days.work: Spread out sun sketches, sundial and moon journal; list three patterns you found.

days.title: Mystery Science sky lesson
days.work: Watch a free Mystery Science sky/spaceship-Earth lesson and answer its mystery question in a sentence.

days.title: Sky Patterns book, part 1
days.work: Make pages about the sun's daily path and the moon's monthly shapes, with drawings from your data.

days.title: Sky Patterns book, part 2
days.work: Add a page about stars at night and a 'What I predict for tonight' page; share the book with family.

days.title: Unit 4 check
days.work: Complete a sky-pattern assessment: order sun positions, sequence moon phases, and explain why stars aren't seen by day.

weeks.assessment: Unit 4 assessment and Sky Patterns book.

objectives: Collect sunrise and sunset times
Count hours of daylight
materials: printed sunrise/sunset times (weather service or newspaper)

days.title: Record times
days.work: Record today's sunrise and sunset times from a weather website and check whether it is dark at dinnertime.

days.title: Count the hours
days.work: Move the hand on a paper clock from sunrise to sunset hour by hour to count daylight hours.

days.title: Summer comparison
days.work: Look up sunrise and sunset for June 21 in your city and count those daylight hours.

days.title: Bar graph
days.work: Make a 2-bar graph comparing winter and summer daylight hours on grid paper.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain which season has more daylight and how your graph shows it.

objectives: Relate the amount of daylight to the time of year
materials: library book on seasons (e.g., 'Sunshine Makes the Seasons' by Franklyn Branley)

days.title: Read about seasons
days.work: Read 'Sunshine Makes the Seasons' (Branley) or a similar library book and list one daylight fact per season.

days.title: Lamp-and-globe model
days.work: Walk a tilted globe around a lamp and notice that your area gets more light in summer and less in winter.

days.title: Season chart
days.work: Make a 4-box chart showing daylight, weather and clothing for each season using monthly sunrise/sunset data.

days.title: Plan the day
days.work: Plan when you could play outside after dinner in December vs. June and explain why the plans differ.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Match 8 cards (long days, short days, months, activities) to the correct season.

objectives: Explain the yearly pattern of daylight with evidence

days.title: Update data
days.work: Record this week's sunrise/sunset and add it to your daylight graph; notice daylight growing since winter.

days.title: NASA Space Place seasons
days.work: Complete a NASA Space Place seasons activity and write one sentence about what you learned.

days.title: Seasons wheel
days.work: Make a paper-plate seasons wheel with a spinner showing daylight length and a picture for each season.

days.title: Present
days.work: Use the wheel to teach a family member how daylight changes through the year.

days.title: Unit 5 check
days.work: Daylight assessment: read a daylight graph, name the longest/shortest season, and predict next month's daylight.

weeks.topic: Animal external parts and their jobs
objectives: Identify animal parts and how they help animals survive
materials: rice, gummy worms, water in a cup, marbles

days.title: Parts and jobs
days.work: Match photos of claws, beaks, shells, fins and ears to the job each does (grab, eat, protect, swim, hear).

days.title: Bird beak lab
days.work: Use tweezers, a clothespin, a spoon and chopsticks as 'beaks' to pick up rice, gummy worms and marbles; record which beak works best for each food.

days.title: Protection parts
days.work: Compare photos of a turtle shell, porcupine quills and an armadillo; tell how each part protects the animal.

days.title: Moving parts
days.work: Compare fins, wings, flippers and legs; act out how each animal moves and say what part helps.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw an animal, label 3 external parts and write what each does.

weeks.topic: Plant external parts and their jobs
objectives: Identify plant parts and how they help plants survive

days.title: Plant dissection
days.work: Take apart a weed or flower and tape roots, stem, leaves and flower onto paper with labels.

days.title: Celery lab
days.work: Put a celery stalk in blue-colored water; check after 4 hours and next morning to see how the stem carries water.

days.title: Root pull
days.work: Pull up a weed and a grass clump; compare roots and explain how roots hold plants and take in water.

days.title: Plant protection
days.work: Look closely (safely) at rose thorns or cactus spines and discuss how they protect the plant from animals.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Plant-parts quiz: label a diagram and match each part to its job.

objectives: Identify human inventions inspired by plant and animal parts
Define a problem to solve

days.title: Velcro and burrs
days.work: Compare Velcro and a burr under a magnifier; draw the tiny hooks on both.

days.title: Invention match
days.work: Match inventions (bike helmet, swim fins, sun hat, tweezers) to the animal or plant part they copy (turtle shell, duck feet, leaves, bird beak).

days.title: Define a problem
days.work: Choose a human problem: keeping your head safe, staying cool in the sun, or picking up tiny things; draw the problem.

days.title: Brainstorm
days.work: List animal or plant parts that solve a similar problem in nature for your chosen problem.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain one biomimicry example in two sentences: the nature part and the invention.

objectives: Sketch and build a solution that mimics a plant or animal part
materials: cardboard, tape, foil, sponges, paper plates

days.title: Two sketches
days.work: Sketch two designs for your problem inspired by an animal or plant part (e.g., a shell-shaped egg protector).

days.title: Choose and plan
days.work: Choose one design and list materials you need; explain why its shape will work.

days.title: Build
days.work: Build the prototype from household materials.

days.title: Label
days.work: Label the prototype's parts and write which nature part each copies.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the prototype to family and use a 4-item design checklist to self-check.

objectives: Test two designs and compare results
Improve a design using data

days.title: Test design A
days.work: Run 3 trials with your first design (e.g., drop the protected egg from 30 cm, 60 cm, 90 cm) and record results.

days.title: Test design B
days.work: Build a quick version of your second sketch and run the same 3 trials.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Make a T-chart of strengths and weaknesses for each design using your data.

days.title: Improve
days.work: Change one thing on the better design and test it again.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write or dictate what you changed, why, and whether the data improved.

weeks.assessment: Test data table and improvement reflection.

objectives: Explain how plants and animals use external parts to survive and inspire inventions

days.title: Mystery Science
days.work: Watch a free Mystery Science animal-parts or plant-parts lesson and answer the mystery question.

days.title: Backyard field guide
days.work: Find 4 plants or animals outside (birds, insects, weeds) and draw each with one labeled survival part.

days.title: Guess the animal
days.work: Play 'Guess the animal from its parts' with a family member using clues like 'webbed feet and a flat bill'.

days.title: Share the guide
days.work: Present your field guide and explain one part that could inspire a new invention.

days.title: Unit 6 check
days.work: Assessment: match parts to functions and explain one biomimicry design.

weeks.topic: How animal parents care for their young
objectives: Identify parent behaviors that help offspring survive
materials: 'Are You My Mother?' by P.D. Eastman (library)
PBS LearningMedia Wild Kratts or nature clips

days.title: Read Are You My Mother?
days.work: Read the story and list what the baby bird needs from its mother.

days.title: Penguin parents
days.work: Watch a PBS clip of emperor penguins and list 3 ways parents keep chicks warm and fed.

days.title: Feeding young
days.work: Compare how birds (bring worms), mammals (milk) and some fish (guard eggs) care for young on a chart.

days.title: Protecting young
days.work: Read about kangaroo pouches and crocodiles carrying babies in their mouths; draw one.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Sort 12 behavior cards into feed, protect, keep warm, or teach.

weeks.topic: How young animals help themselves survive
objectives: Identify offspring behaviors that signal needs or keep them safe
materials: 'Make Way for Ducklings' by Robert McCloskey (library)

days.title: Calling for help
days.work: Listen to recordings (PBS or library) of baby birds chirping and kittens mewing; tell what each baby is asking for.

days.title: Follow the leader
days.work: Read 'Make Way for Ducklings' and explain why the ducklings stay in a line behind their mother.

days.title: Learning by copying
days.work: Read about bear cubs and young chimpanzees learning to find food by watching parents.

days.title: Interview
days.work: Interview a parent about how you signaled your needs as a baby and how they responded; record 3 answers.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain one offspring behavior and how it helps the baby survive, in two sentences.

weeks.topic: Patterns in parent and offspring behavior
objectives: Find patterns across many kinds of animals

days.title: Pattern chart
days.work: Make a chart of 6 animals with columns for 'what parents do' and 'what babies do'.

days.title: Find patterns
days.work: Circle behaviors that appear for many animals (feeding, protecting, calling) and state one pattern.

days.title: Mini-book draft
days.work: Write a 4-page mini-book about one animal family (e.g., robins) with a fact on each page.

days.title: Share
days.work: Read your mini-book aloud and answer two questions from a listener.

days.title: Unit 7 check
days.work: Assessment: read a short passage about a new animal and identify parent and offspring behaviors.

weeks.topic: Young animals are like their parents
objectives: Compare traits of young animals and their parents

days.title: Match the families
days.work: Match 10 baby animal photos to their parents and name one trait that gave it away.

days.title: Puppy and dog Venn
days.work: Compare a puppy and its parent in a Venn diagram: ears, fur color, size, tail.

days.title: Not exactly alike
days.work: Look at a photo of a litter of kittens and list differences between the kittens and their mother.

days.title: Family photos
days.work: Compare photos of yourself, siblings and parents; find 2 shared traits and 2 differences.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write 'Young animals are like their parents because... but not exactly because...' with evidence.

weeks.topic: Young plants are like their parents
objectives: Compare young plants with parent plants
Measure variation
materials: adult plant of the same kind (or photo)

days.title: Seedling vs. adult
days.work: Compare bean seedlings with an adult bean plant photo; list matching leaf shapes and differences in size.

days.title: Measure leaves
days.work: Measure the longest leaf on 5 seedlings in centimeters and record the results.

days.title: Same kind of flower
days.work: Compare 3 flowers from the same plant type (e.g., roses or dandelions); note color and petal differences.

days.title: Plant journal
days.work: Draw and label two seedlings side by side showing how they are alike and different.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an evidence statement about plants being like, but not exactly like, their parents.

weeks.topic: Variation within a kind of animal or plant
objectives: Describe how individuals of the same kind vary

days.title: Dog breeds
days.work: Compare photos of a Chihuahua and a Great Dane; list what makes both dogs and what is different.

days.title: Leaf collection
days.work: Collect 10 leaves from one tree and measure each length with paper clips.

days.title: Leaf graph
days.work: Graph leaf lengths into short, medium and long groups.

days.title: Discuss
days.work: Discuss why leaves on one tree and puppies in one litter are not exactly the same.

days.title: Unit 8 check
days.work: Assessment: compare a parent and offspring picture and explain likenesses and differences.

objectives: Apply science ideas from the year to design a solution
materials: cups, string, flashlight, cardboard, tape, foil

days.title: Choose a problem
days.work: Choose a challenge: send a message across the yard using light or sound, or solve a human problem by copying an animal part.

days.title: Sketch and build
days.work: Sketch two ideas, choose one and build a first prototype.

days.title: Test
days.work: Test the prototype 3 times and record what happened in a simple data table.

days.title: Improve
days.work: Change one feature based on your data and test again.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Get feedback from a family member using 'one thing that works, one thing to try'.

objectives: Communicate results and reflect on a year of investigations

days.title: Notebook review
days.work: Page through your science notebook and flag your 3 favorite investigations.

days.title: Poster
days.work: Make a poster for your showcase project: problem, design sketch, test data and improvement.

days.title: Science fair
days.work: Present the project and one favorite investigation to family, answering their questions.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write or dictate 3 sentences about what you learned about sound, light, sky or living things.

days.title: Year-end check
days.work: Complete a year-end science review of key ideas from each unit.

weeks.assessment: Science fair presentation and year-end review.
